html:
Terra Browser puts the things you do most often into one app. Each of the five tabs at the bottom does one job:

  • Browse: a built-in browser with ad blocking. Save whole pages as offline files and download the images and videos on a page.
  • YouTube: ad-free YouTube and YouTube Music, with background playback and video / music downloads.
  • Summary: hand a YouTube video to the AI to get a transcript, summary and chapters, and ask questions about the video.
  • Library: everything you save lives here. Play videos and music, view PDFs and images, open and edit Word / Excel / PPT / text files.
  • Settings: appearance, ad blocking, passcode lock, downloads, updates, and this manual.

Tap any title below to expand it. To read this again later, go to "App User Manual" at the top of Settings.

The phone asks only when a feature needs a permission; just choose "Allow". You can refuse permissions for features you don't use and everything else keeps working.

PermissionWhat it is for
NotificationsDownload progress, download finished, and playback controls for background music. Recommended; otherwise downloads and music may stop when the screen turns off.
Install unknown appsNeeded when the app updates itself to a new version ("Settings → Version & updates").
MicrophoneOnly when song recognition listens to the sound around you. Not needed to recognize a video or music playing inside the app.
Camera"Scan QR code", and "Intruder photo" (one photo when someone enters the wrong passcode 3 times in a row).
Screen recording, Do Not DisturbNeeded when a video that cannot be downloaded is captured by screen recording; the system asks again each time a recording starts.
Folder access"Auto-import downloads from other apps" needs you to pick that app's download folder once.
FingerprintUse your fingerprint instead of typing the unlock passcode.

Battery settings: some phones close apps running in the background. If music or downloads stop when the screen is off, go to the phone's "Settings → Apps → Terra Browser → Battery" and choose "Unrestricted".

Translate page (AI): on a foreign-language page, open the menu at the top right → "Translate page". The app uses Gemini to translate all the text on the page into your interface language while keeping the layout. When new content appears as you scroll, tap it again to "Translate newly loaded content", or choose "Show original". A Gemini key is required (see "Summary").

Automatic http / https switching: when a page will not open (unreachable or server error), the app automatically retries once with the other protocol: http for sites whose https is broken, https for sites that only work over https.

Scan QR code: "Scan QR code" next to "History" on the home page. Scan with the camera (zoom with the slider, tap "Switch lens" if the phone has several rear cameras, or pick from photos and turn on the flashlight). A web address opens right away in the app; a file-transfer QR code shared from this app saves the files straight into your Library. Camera permission is asked the first time.

Type an address or keywords at the top to browse; ads are blocked automatically. The "Menu" at the top right (grid icon) contains:

  • Capture page: saves the whole page with its images as one offline file in the Library under "Pages", readable without a connection.
  • Download video: detects the images and videos on the page so you can choose format and quality. For videos that cannot be caught, use "Record" instead: record in the background, or play full screen and record with the phone's screen recorder (Do Not Disturb turns on automatically and recording stops when the video ends).
  • Bookmark this page / Bookmark list: add sites you visit often to "My bookmarks", organized in folders.
  • History, Incognito mode (no history, no saved passwords) and Full-screen browsing.
  • Manual cleanup: tap away ads that could not be blocked or blocks you don't want to see.
  • Floating download button: shows or hides the draggable "⬇" button on web pages. If the button has disappeared, turn it off and on again and it returns to the right edge of the screen.

Remember passwords: when you sign in to a site, the app asks at the bottom whether to save the password and fills it in next time. Before the first save you need to set a 6-digit unlock passcode.

Links to YouTube or YouTube Music tapped in the browser open automatically in the "YouTube" tab.

1. Tap the "YouTube" tab at the bottom for YouTube without ads. You can sign in to your own Google account to see your subscriptions.
  2. Background playback: sound keeps playing when you switch apps or turn off the screen; going to the home screen shrinks the video into a small window (picture-in-picture). Picture-in-picture appears only while watching a video on YouTube or a web video in the "Browse" tab, not while listening to YouTube Music.
  3. Download: tap the video and use the "⬇" button on the player control bar to choose a quality, or download only the music (MP3). In Shorts, the download button is at the top right, to the right of the magnifier. Downloaded files are in the Library. (The floating download button is no longer shown on the YouTube tab; it is still there for ordinary pages in "Browse".)
  4. Hand over to another download app: the download panel can also pass the video to apps such as Snaptube; when they finish, the file is moved back into the Library automatically (see "Auto-import downloads from other apps").
  5. Song recognition: the round waveform button at the top. Tap it when you want to know which song is playing in a video; the app listens directly to the video's sound for 10 seconds (no microphone, the video is not paused) and tells you the title (details in the "YouTube Music" section).
  6. "⋮" at the top right opens the player settings: default quality, playback speed, automatic sponsor skipping and more.

1. At the top of the YouTube tab there is a "video / note" switch. Switch to the note for YouTube Music.
  2. Tap any song to play it and open the player panel: cover, progress bar, previous / next, shuffle, repeat and the play queue. The "⬇" to the right of the title downloads the song.
  3. Lyrics: tap "Lyrics" in the player panel. The app looks for synced lyrics that follow the singing; if none are found it shows YouTube Music's own lyrics. You can also tap "Find lyrics" and choose yourself.
  4. After you close the panel, a small player bar stays at the bottom for pause and next; ✕ on the far right stops playback.
  5. Song recognition: the round waveform button next to the switch (on both YouTube and YouTube Music). It listens for 10 seconds and identifies the song.
    · Something is playing in the app: it listens to that sound directly, without the microphone, and playback is not paused.
    · Nothing is playing, or you tap "Listen to the surroundings instead": it uses the microphone to hear music around you (from other apps or speakers too).
    · In YouTube Music it searches for the song automatically; while watching a YouTube video it only shows the title, the video keeps playing, and you tap to search if you want.
    This feature needs a Gemini key (see "Summary").
  6. The phone's notification shade and quick panel also show the current song, and you can control playback from there.

Let the AI watch a YouTube video and pick out the key points for you. First get a free Gemini key (API key) — you only do this once:

  1. Open aistudio.google.com in a browser and sign in with your Google account.
  2. Tap "Get API key" → "Create API key".
  3. A long string of letters and digits appears; tap "Copy".
  4. Back in this app, tap the "Summary" tab at the bottom, then the button at the top right that shows the AI name, to open "AI settings".
  5. Choose "Gemini" as the AI engine and paste the key into the "Gemini API key" field.

Once it is set up:

  • Paste a YouTube URL in "Summary", or tap "Share" in the YouTube app / this app's YouTube tab → choose "AI Summary (Terra Browser)".
  • The AI produces a transcript, summary and chapters; "Dialogue" lets you ask questions about the video. For videos without subtitles the AI watches the video and transcribes it.
  • Analysis can run in the background (you can turn off the screen or switch apps) and notifies you when done; tapping the notification opens that video directly. Analyzed videos are kept in folders by channel.
  • Check unfinished: the button to the right of the "Analyzed videos" heading. It finds videos with no transcript, or no summary and chapters. You can "Catch up on the phone" (re-runs them one by one; swiping the app away from the recent-apps list interrupts it) or "Hand to GitHub cloud".
  • GitHub cloud: "⋮" at the top right → "GitHub cloud". Paste a GitHub token with the repo and workflow permissions (created the same way as for cross-network transfer, but tick these two). The app creates a private repository terra-ai-cloud on your GitHub and stores your Gemini key there encrypted. Videos handed to the cloud keep running even with the screen off or the app fully closed, and the results are fetched automatically the next time you open the app. You can also turn on "Send new videos straight to the cloud".
  • Storage used: the top of the Summary home page shows how much space all transcripts and summaries take; "⋮" next to each video shows that video's size. Transcripts and summaries are all kept on the phone and never deleted automatically.

The key is stored only on your phone. Gemini's free quota has a daily limit and resets the next day; if you avoid the models marked "paid" in the list you will not be charged. In "AI settings" you can also switch to Claude (needs your own Claude subscription or API key); leaving that unset is fine.

• Categories: files are sorted automatically by type into Pages, PDF, Images, Videos, Music, Word, Excel, APK, EXE and more. "Categories" at the far right of the category bar lets you rename, reorder and add your own; for your own categories you can set file extensions (e.g. apk) so files of that type are collected there automatically. To move a file to another category: long-press to select → "Move to another category" in the toolbar (stacked-squares icon); the folder icon beside it moves files into a folder inside the same category.
  • Opening a category: Videos, Music, Pages, Images, PDF, Word, Excel, PPT, Text files, Subtitles, Archives. Tap a category at the top to open it.
  • Import files from the phone: tap "＋"; you can pick many at once and the app sorts them into the right category by extension.
  • Music: an offline music player with playlists, shuffle, repeat and synced lyrics.
  • Videos: a built-in player with subtitles, speed control and seeking.
  • Word / Excel / PPT / text files: tap to view; tap "Edit" to change text or cells and save. PPT files can be shown as a slideshow. Macro-enabled Excel files show their macro code and keep the macros intact, but macros cannot run on a phone.
  • Organize: long-press files to multi-select, then move to a folder, rename or delete. Deleted files go to the trash first.
  • Duplicate file alert: when a newly added file has the same name or size as an existing one, you are asked whether to keep both, rename, or delete.
  • Send to a computer or another phone: "Settings → Storage & export → Wireless transfer to PC / phone". The other person scans the QR code on screen (or types the link) and downloads in a browser. Both sides need to be behind the same router (Wi-Fi or cable); with no shared network, turn on this phone's "Personal hotspot" for them to join, or use USB tethering. If they are on a completely different network, use a relay (see "Cross-network transfer").

When the other person is not on your network (they are somewhere else, or you only have mobile data), files can go through a "relay" first. There are two kinds:

GitHub relayPublic relay
Where files passYour own GitHub accountA public relay run by someone else (ppng.io by default)
Stored?Temporarily; deleted after the transferNo, they only pass through live
When they can downloadAny time (until deleted)Both online at the same time; keep your screen open
PreparationA GitHub account and tokenNone

Both kinds encrypt the files on the phone first. The decryption key exists only in the link you give the other person; neither the relay nor anyone else can open the files.

How to use

  1. In the Library, long-press to tick the files to send → "Export / Share" → "Wireless transfer to PC / phone".
  2. Choose "GitHub relay" or "Public relay" at the top.
  3. Let the other person scan the QR code, or tap "Send to them" to pass the link via a messaging app. They open it in a browser and download; no app needed.
  4. If they also have this app: they tap "Scan QR code" on the Browse home page (or paste the link into the address bar) and the files are downloaded, decrypted and saved straight into their Library.

GitHub relay: set up a token the first time

  1. Sign in to github.com in a browser (register for free if you have no account).
  2. Profile picture at the top right → Settings → Developer settings at the bottom left → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic).
  3. Tap Generate new token (classic). Note: anything (e.g. "Terra Browser transfer"); Expiration: your choice; under permissions tick only public_repo.
  4. Tap Generate token at the bottom and copy the string starting with ghp_ (it is shown only once).
  5. Back in the app, paste it on the "GitHub relay" tab and tap "Save and check". The app creates a public repository named web-saver-relay on your GitHub to act as the relay.

GitHub relay: delete after the transfer  When they have finished downloading, tap "They got it, delete temporary copy" to remove the temporary files from GitHub. If you forget, the app deletes them automatically after 60 minutes (the app must be open).

Very large files (over 300 MB) are slow through a relay; transfer them directly over the same network or a phone hotspot instead. The public relay is someone else's free service and may occasionally be unreachable; use the GitHub relay when that happens.

Some videos are easier to get with other download apps (such as Snaptube or Quetta). After a one-time setup, the videos, music and subtitles they download are moved into this app's Library automatically and the original files deleted, so nothing takes up space twice.

  1. Install that download app first and download any file with it (so that its download folder exists).
  2. Go to "Settings → Image & video downloads → Auto-import downloads from other apps".
  3. Choose the app, tap the add-folder button, find its download folder in the screen that appears (usually "Download" or a folder named after the app), then tap "Use this folder" → "Allow". If videos and music go to separate folders, add both.
  4. From then on, choose "Hand to Snaptube to download" (or another app) in YouTube's download panel. When the download finishes and you come back to this app, the file appears in the Library automatically.

The app checks once whenever it returns to the foreground, and every 15 seconds for 3 hours after handing a download to another app. To check right away, tap "Refresh" in the Library.

• Go to "Settings → Privacy & security → Passcode lock & fingerprint" to set a 6-digit passcode; fingerprint unlock can be turned on as well.
  • You can lock: saved passwords, a whole Library category (e.g. Videos), a single folder, and My bookmarks.
  • After unlocking once you are not asked again until the app is closed; you can also tap "Lock now".
  • Three wrong attempts in a row take a photo with the front camera (camera permission required); photos are kept in a locked folder.

Remember your unlock passcode. It is stored only on this phone; if you forget it nobody can recover it and the locked content cannot be opened.

The interface is written in Traditional Chinese. "語言 Language" at the top of Settings (there is also a button at the top of this manual) switches to English, 日本語, 한국어, 简体中文, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, Bahasa Indonesia, Español, Français, Deutsch and more.

  • English, 日本語, 한국어, 简体中文: built in. They switch instantly, with no key and no waiting.
  • Other languages: the first time you choose one, Gemini translates the interface and the manual once (set a Gemini key first, see "Summary"). It takes about 1–3 minutes with progress shown on screen; the result is stored on the phone and never needs translating again.
  • To switch back: choose "繁體中文" in the same place.
Only interface text is translated; your file names, song titles and bookmark titles are never changed. A few places (text in the system notification shade, button hints on the YouTube player) are still in Chinese for now.

• "Settings → Version & updates" checks for new versions. Small updates are applied directly; big updates download a new installer — just tap "Install" (the first time you need to allow "Install unknown apps").
  • On the same page you can share the app's download link with friends.

• Music or downloads stop when the screen is off: allow notifications and set this app's battery setting to "Unrestricted".
  • Summary says the quota is used up: the free Gemini quota for the day is gone; try again tomorrow, or pick another model in "AI settings".
  • A YouTube video fails to download: reload the video and try again; if it still fails, download it with another app from the download panel.
  • Files downloaded by other apps were not moved back: make sure the correct download folder was added, then tap "Refresh" in the Library.
  • Cannot find a file: type its name in the search box at the top of the Library; also check locked categories and the trash.
